# Routing

An intent as given, the references extracted from its text, the protocol the router proposes for it, and the slice run that works the intent until it is blocked. A pick is a proposal, never authority.

`intake.routing` is one of intake's bounded contexts. [All domains](./index.mdx).

## Types

### `AcceptedRoute`

`intake.routing.AcceptedRoute` is a record of five fields:

- `protocol` — `String`
- `intent_revision` — `String`
- `catalog` — `List<intake.routing.CatalogDigest>`
- `context_policy` — `intake.context.ContextPolicy`
- `threshold` — `Decimal`

### `ActionRequestId`

`intake.routing.ActionRequestId` wraps `Uuid` and is not interchangeable with one: the whole value of naming it separately is the crossings the model then refuses.

### `AgentRevisionId`

`intake.routing.AgentRevisionId` wraps `Uuid` and is not interchangeable with one: the whole value of naming it separately is the crossings the model then refuses.

### `CaseId`

`intake.routing.CaseId` wraps `String` and is not interchangeable with one: the whole value of naming it separately is the crossings the model then refuses.

### `CatalogDigest`

`intake.routing.CatalogDigest` is a record of two fields:

- `name` — `String`
- `digest` — `String`

### `CommissionId`

`intake.routing.CommissionId` wraps `Uuid` and is not interchangeable with one: the whole value of naming it separately is the crossings the model then refuses.

### `IntentId`

`intake.routing.IntentId` wraps `Uuid` and is not interchangeable with one: the whole value of naming it separately is the crossings the model then refuses.

### `ReferenceKind`

`intake.routing.ReferenceKind` is one of `JiraIssue`, `SlackMessage`, `GitlabIssue`, `GitlabMergeRequest`, `GithubIssue`, `GithubPullRequest` and `Url`.

### `StopReason`

`intake.routing.StopReason` is one of `ApprovalRequired`, `NothingAdmissible`, `StepBudget`, `NoLocalExecutor`, `Refused`, `ConfinementUnavailable` and `Completed`.

## Entities

An entity is what this context is about: something with an identity that outlives any one request, a shape, and a lifecycle. The lifecycle is exhaustive — a move that is not drawn below is a move this specification does not permit, and that is the only way it says so. Every move is labelled with the command that takes it, because a move nothing can trigger is refused rather than drawn.

### `ExtractedReference`

`intake.routing.ExtractedReference`.

An instance is identified by `reference_id`, a `Uuid`. The name is part of the model and not a convention: a view projects the identity under that name, so a projection inventing its own would disagree with the view.

It holds:

- `intent_id` — `intake.routing.IntentId`
- `kind` — `intake.routing.ReferenceKind`
- `value` — `String`

Its `intent_id` is what [`Intent`](#intent) owns it by, as `references`.

No invariant is declared, so nothing here constrains an instance at rest.

Its state is a `intake.routing.ExtractedReference.State`, one of `Extracted`. That enum is synthesised from the lifecycle rather than declared beside it, so the states a view's filter compares and the states drawn below cannot disagree.

An instance is created in `Extracted`. `Extracted` is terminal, so an instance may rest there forever. That is declared rather than inferred from having no way out: an entity that cannot leave a state is either finished or stuck, and only its author knows which.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Extracted
    Extracted --> [*]
```

It declares no moves, so nothing changes its state once it exists.

It has one state, so there is no move to permit or to forbid.

No view projects it, so nothing outside this context is promised a way to observe one.

## Commands

### `DropResumeContext`

`intake.routing.DropResumeContext`.

It takes:

- `commission_id` — `intake.routing.CommissionId`

It has three outcomes.

**`dropped`** — The default branch, taken when no other outcome's condition matched. It removes the `intake.routing.ResumeContext` its input names; no view shows it afterwards. The instance is the one named by the input field `commission_id`. It emits nothing. A test reaches it by constructing an input that satisfies no other outcome's condition.

**`not-found`** — Taken when the identity the command names is one no record carries, before any other answer for it. No entity in this specification changes. It reports `intake.routing.ResumeContextNotFound`, carrying `commission_id`. It emits nothing. A test reaches it by sending an identity no record carries, arranging nothing.

**`storage-failed`** — Decided outside the input: the resume context store cannot remove the context. No predicate over the input reaches this branch, and saying `when: false` instead would have claimed it is unreachable, which is a different and false statement. No entity in this specification changes. It reports `intake.routing.ResumeContextStorageFailed`, carrying `reason`. It emits nothing. A test reaches it by injecting the declared fault, because no input can.

### `RecordMergeHandoff`

`intake.routing.RecordMergeHandoff`.

It takes:

- `action_request_id` — `intake.routing.ActionRequestId`
- `commission_id` — `intake.routing.CommissionId`
- `workspace` — `String`
- `head` — `String`

It has three outcomes.

**`already-recorded`** — Taken when a record already carries the identity the command's creating branch would create, and no input-guarded refusal applies. No entity in this specification changes. It reports `intake.routing.MergeHandoffAlreadyRecorded`, carrying `action_request_id`. It emits nothing. A test reaches it by sending the command twice with one identity: the first call creates the record, the second is answered by this branch.

**`recorded`** — The default branch, taken when no other outcome's condition matched. It creates a `intake.routing.MergeHandoff`, which starts in `Recorded`. The new instance's identity is published as `action_request_id` on `intake.routing.MergeHandedOff`. It emits `intake.routing.MergeHandedOff`. It sets `commission_id` from `input.commission_id`, `workspace` from `input.workspace` and `head` from `input.head`. A test reaches it by constructing an input that satisfies no other outcome's condition.

**`storage-failed`** — Decided outside the input: the state directory cannot record the hand-off. No predicate over the input reaches this branch, and saying `when: false` instead would have claimed it is unreachable, which is a different and false statement. No entity in this specification changes. It reports `intake.routing.MergeHandoffStorageFailed`, carrying `reason`. It emits nothing. A test reaches it by injecting the declared fault, because no input can.

## Events

### `MergeHandedOff`

`intake.routing.MergeHandedOff`.

It carries:

- `action_request_id` — `intake.routing.ActionRequestId`
- `commission_id` — `intake.routing.CommissionId`
- `workspace` — `String`
- `head` — `String`

Emitted by `intake.routing.RecordMergeHandoff` on its `recorded` outcome.

Nothing in this system reacts to it.

## Errors

### `MergeHandoffAlreadyRecorded`

It carries:

- `action_request_id` — `intake.routing.ActionRequestId`

Reported by `intake.routing.RecordMergeHandoff` on its `already-recorded` outcome.

### `MergeHandoffStorageFailed`

It carries:

- `reason` — `String`

Reported by `intake.routing.RecordMergeHandoff` on its `storage-failed` outcome.

### `ResumeContextNotFound`

It carries:

- `commission_id` — `intake.routing.CommissionId`

Reported by `intake.routing.DropResumeContext` on its `not-found` outcome.

### `ResumeContextStorageFailed`

It carries:

- `reason` — `String`

Reported by `intake.routing.DropResumeContext` on its `storage-failed` outcome.
